subject: MedSync follow-up: DPA points (controller/processor, retention, logs)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julia Chen <julia.chen@medsync.health>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-11-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo recap + DPA clarifications you asked for

Hi Julia / Aaron —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap and the asks you requested so it's easy to track: 

1) Roles: You asked whether Redwood is a processor for request/response inference where MedSync supplies patient data and controls prompts/labels. Short answer: for the hosting mode you described (MedSync controls dataset and legal purpose), Redwood will sign on as a processor in the DPA and act under your documented instructions. We can annotate the DPA to make that explicit.

2) Subprocessors: You asked about which third parties may have access to logs/metrics. I attached our current subprocessor list and the SOC2 snapshot for context. We commit to notify customers 30 days in advance of onboarding any new subprocessors with access to customer data (subject to contract).

3) Retention / logs: You wanted a 90-day maximum for application logs and 30-day for debug-level request traces containing PII. We can offer configurable retention windows by account tier; default hosted retention is 180 days but we can contractually limit to 90/30 for this deal.

4) Breach notice / timelines: Our standard DPA has a 72-hour notification clause for confirmed incidents; you asked whether this covers subprocessor incidents affecting your data. Yes, we treat subprocessor incidents as our responsibility for notification under the DPA. 

Next steps I propose:
- Monica to confirm the 30/90 retention/notification language and provide exact clause text.
- I will upload a redline of the DPA and confirm whether we can add the 30-day subprocessor notice commitment.
- If that looks good, Julia / Aaron to confirm procurement timeline and whether MedSync needs us on an upcoming vendor security review on 11/18.

Attachments: MedSync_DPA_Redwood_redline_v1.pdf (redline), SOC2-snapshot-2027-09.pdf

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0142

From: Julia Chen <julia.chen@medsync.health>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aaron Patel <aaron.patel@medsync.health>
Date: 2027-11-09T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + DPA clarifications you asked for

Thanks, Aditya — very helpful. A couple of clarifying questions before we loop in procurement/security: 

- On the controller/processor callout: can Redwood add a short definition in the DPA for the inference context ("Redwood will process data as a processor when customer supplies PII as part of inference requests and customer sets the processing purpose"). We can share our legal's suggested language but wanted to check if Redwood is open to that exact phrasing.

- For retention: MedSync needs to ensure that debug traces that include raw prompts (which may include PHI in our workflows) are purged within 30 days and are not included in analytics exports. Can you confirm design + enforcement?

- Subprocessor notifications: we typically ask for a 45-day advance notice. Is that flexible? If not, we need to understand the exception process (for critical infra providers).

We have an initial vendor security review scheduled 2027-11-18; Aaron will coordinate.

Julia Chen
VP Product & Data Governance | MedSync Health
julia.chen@medsync.health

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julia Chen <julia.chen@medsync.health>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-11-10T08:26:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + DPA clarifications you asked for

Hi Julia / Aaron —

Thanks for the clear asks. Quick responses from security/legal side below; I've included exact clause language proposals you can cut/paste into your redline.

1) Controller/Processor wording (proposed DPA insertion):
"For the purposes of this Addendum, when Customer supplies personal data to Redwood Inference to initiate inference requests or to evaluate outputs, Customer is the Controller and Redwood is the Processor acting on the Customer's documented instructions. Redwood shall process such personal data only on behalf of and under the documented instructions of Customer."

2) Retention and export controls (proposed):
"Redwood will retain application logs for a maximum of 90 days and debug-level request traces (including raw prompts and outputs) for a maximum of 30 days for the Customer account identified in Exhibit A. Redwood will not include raw debug traces in analytics exports or third-party reporting unless explicitly authorized in writing by the Customer."

3) Subprocessor notice:
"Redwood will provide Customer with at least 30 days' prior notice of the engagement of any new subprocessor that will have access to Customer's personal data. For subprocessors engaged for urgent security or critical infrastructure reasons, Redwood will provide notice as soon as practicable and will offer written justification; such engagements will be subject to Customer's audit rights as set out in Section X."

Notes: 
- Your 45-day ask is longer than our standard 30-day notice. We can agree to 45 days for business-critical subprocessors if MedSync includes that in Exhibit A as an account-level requirement; otherwise 30 days is the standard we offer.
- Enforcement: the retention windows will be configurable at the account level; we'll include a Service Level for retention enforcement and an auditable logging endpoint (metadata only) for proof of deletion.

I've attached the SOC2 snapshot and a short redline that applies the proposed wording. Happy to hop on call with your legal team if that helps.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Head of Security & Trust | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: SOC2-snapshot-2027-09.pdf

From: Julia Chen <julia.chen@medsync.health>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aaron Patel <aaron.patel@medsync.health>
Date: 2027-11-10T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + DPA clarifications you asked for

Monica — this is great and gets us most of the way there. A few follow-ups: 

- The proposed controller/processor sentence looks fine; our counsel will run it but I don't expect changes.
- For subprocessors: MedSync is willing to accept 30 days as a baseline if Redwood agrees to provide an internal escalation path and an SLA for justification docs when a subprocessor is onboarded under an urgent exception. Can Redwood commit to a written explanation within 3 business days of such an urgent onboarding?

- For retention enforcement proof: can you share a sample deletion log (metadata-only) format so our legal/security can validate it during review? Even a 1-page example is fine.

Assuming we get that, procurement will draft PO language. We need a target execution date of 2027-11-26 to align with our rollout.

Thanks,
Julia

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julia Chen <julia.chen@medsync.health>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aaron Patel <aaron.patel@medsync.health>
Date: 2027-11-12T16:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + DPA clarifications you asked for

Hi Julia / Aaron —

Thanks for the quick turn. A few operational confirmations from infra/ops: 

- Urgent subprocessor onboarding: Redwood will post a written justification to the customer portal within 3 business days for any urgent subprocessor event. We'll also log a change record (ID / timestamp / scope) and offer a one-time technical review with our security team within 10 business days.

- Deletion proof sample: attached below is a sample metadata-only deletion log (JSON lines) format that we can provide via the secure portal or as part of an audit package. Example line (metadata-only):
{timestamp: "2027-11-12T15:09:22Z", account_id: "MS-89012", record_type: "debug_trace", record_id: "dtrc-39a2", deletion_method: "scheduled_purge", retention_policy_applied: "30d"}

- Execution target: Aditya / I can support accelerated contract review. If MedSync signals green by 2027-11-18 we can route to legal and aim for 2027-11-26 execution but that will require both sides to turn quickly on final DPA redlines and PO approvals.

Next step for Redwood: I'll upload the sample deletion log to the secure share and update the redline with the controller/processor sentence Monica proposed. Aditya will follow up on procurement dates.

Best,
Priyom Das
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: sample-deletion-log-line.txt (metadata-only example)
